title: Visual Space Perception and Visually Directed Action

findings.antecedent: depth intervals on the ground plane compared to frontal intervals at the same distance
findings.source: text, page 1, and Exp 1 Results, page 5
findings.quote: The depth intervals had to be made considerably larger than the frontal intervals to appear equal in length

findings.antecedent: egocentric distance of the intervals (4 m-12 m)
findings.consequent: physical inequality of equal-appearing intervals (degree of foreshortening)
findings.source: text, page 1, and Exp 1 Results, page 5
findings.quote: this physical inequality of equal-appearing intervals increasing with egocentric distance of the intervals (4 m-12 m).

findings.mechanism: visually directed action is accurate and near-linear
findings.quote: The corresponding power function exponents were .98 and .96, indicating near-linearity of the responses.

findings.antecedent: walking to a single target (width condition)
findings.mechanism: visually directed action is accurate with slight undershoot
findings.quote: mean signed error was -27 cm (undershoot) and the mean absolute error was 57 cm

findings.antecedent: walking to a single target (depth condition)
findings.mechanism: visually directed action is accurate with slight undershoot
findings.quote: in the depth condition, the mean signed error was -50 cm (undershoot) and the mean absolute error was 74 cm.

findings.antecedent: walking to two targets to mark an interval
findings.mechanism: some inaccuracy in the walking response (overestimation)
findings.quote: the mean intervals were on the average about 50 cm larger than the corresponding physical intervals

findings.antecedent: frontal intervals vs sagittal intervals (for walking to two targets)
findings.mechanism: visually directed action does not manifest perceptual anisotropy
findings.quote: walking to two targets does not manifest this anisotropy

findings.antecedent: blind pointing toward a previously viewed target (no vision condition)
findings.consequent: mean absolute error in pointing direction

findings.antecedent: pointing toward a continuously viewed target (vision condition)
findings.consequent: mean absolute error in pointing direction

findings.antecedent: walking blindly past a previously viewed target (100 cm path)
findings.consequent: angular velocity of the arm (pointing direction)
findings.mechanism: imaginal updating of some internal spatial representation
findings.quote: the angular velocity of the arm (given by the slope of the function) changes systematically during the traverse in accord with the true target azimuth.

stimuli.description: white steel rods (16 cm high, 1 cm diameter) on a grassy field for walking and matching tasks.
red neon lamp on the ground in a lightproof warehouse (35m x 20m) for pointing task.

limitations: The paper discusses potential limitations or confounding factors in *other* studies (e.g., Böök & Gärling, 1981) when trying to reconcile findings, such as reduced cue availability in darkened rooms, interference from specific procedures (moving light strip), or the use of verbal responses vs. motoric responses. However, it does not explicitly state limitations for its own experiments' methodology.
